title: Production shape
goal: Set the quality bar once, on one service, while it is small. Errors, configuration, tests and logs. Everything you do here you will repeat in eight more services, so it is worth doing slowly.
startWith: Step 02 finished: the service reads accounts from Postgres and one Testcontainers test passes.

newIdeas.plain: A small agreed JSON shape for API errors — type, title, status, detail — served as application/problem+json. Spring builds it for you via ProblemDetail. It means callers can handle your errors without parsing prose.
A class where you put exception handlers that apply to every controller, so error mapping lives in one place instead of in try/catch blocks.
Binds a whole block of configuration onto a typed record and validates it at startup. Compare with @Value("${...}") scattered over ten classes, where a typo is found at 3am rather than at boot.
Starts only the web layer — controllers, JSON mapping, error handling — with the database and everything else absent. Fast, and it fails for exactly one reason.

Log lines as JSON objects rather than sentences, so a log system can filter on fields. Add a request id to every line and one user request becomes greppable across services — which matters enormously from step 04 onward.

tasks.do: Return RFC 9457 problem details instead of stack traces
tasks.why: An unhandled exception currently leaks your class names to the caller and gives them nothing to act on.
tasks.how: Add one advice class. ProblemDetail is built into Spring, so there is no library to add. Throw a domain exception from the application layer and map it here; the controller stays free of error plumbing.

blocks.label: domain/model/AccountNotFoundException.java
adapter/in/web/ApiExceptionHandler.java
Make the controller throw instead of returning 404 by hand

check.expect: 404 with Content-Type: application/problem+json and a type URI — not a stack trace.

tasks.do: Move configuration onto a validated @ConfigurationProperties record
tasks.why: Configuration mistakes should stop the application at startup, not surface as a null three hours later.
tasks.how: Add spring-boot-starter-validation, then bind a record. @Validated plus the Jakarta constraints mean a missing or nonsensical value fails the boot with a readable message naming the property.

blocks.label: config/AccountProperties.java
application.yml — add the block
blocks.body:
ledgerflow:
  account:
    display-name: LedgerFlow Account
    max-wallets-per-account: 500

check.run: # temporarily blank display-name in application.yml and start the app
check.expect: Startup fails with a message naming ledgerflow.account.display-name. Put the value back.

tasks.do: Write a domain unit test with no Spring and no database
tasks.why: The rules that matter should be testable in milliseconds. If testing a business rule needs a container, the rule is in the wrong place.
tasks.how: This test imports nothing from Spring. It runs in the time it takes to read this sentence. Aim for most of your tests to look like this and only a few to need containers.

blocks.label: src/test/java/io/ledgerflow/account/domain/model/AccountTest.java

check.expect: Green, in well under a second, with no Docker involved.

tasks.do: Add a @WebMvcTest slice test for the controller
tasks.why: It checks the HTTP layer — routing, JSON, error mapping — without paying for a database.
tasks.how: The repository is replaced with a Mockito stub via @MockitoBean (Boot 3.4+ name; the old @MockBean is deprecated). Mind the import: Boot 4 moved @WebMvcTest out of boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet into boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure, so a 3.x snippet fails with Cannot resolve symbol 'web' - the package, not the annotation, is what is missing. You now have three test layers: domain unit tests, this web slice, and the Testcontainers integration test from step 02.

blocks.label: src/test/java/io/ledgerflow/account/adapter/in/web/AccountControllerTest.java

tasks.do: Expose health and serve an OpenAPI document
tasks.why: Health endpoints are what Kubernetes will call in step 16, and an OpenAPI document is how the next service will learn your API in step 05.
tasks.how: Actuator is already a dependency. Add springdoc for the OpenAPI document — Spring Boot does not generate one on its own. Keep the exposed endpoint list explicit: exposing everything by accident is a common way to publish your environment variables.

blocks.label: pom.xml — paste inside <dependencies>
blocks.body:
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springdoc</groupId>
  <artifactId>springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui</artifactId>
  <version>3.0.3</version>   <!-- the 3.x line is the Boot 4 one -->
</dependency>

blocks.label: application.yml — add the block
blocks.body:
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,metrics
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: always

blocks.label: Check both
blocks.body:
curl -s localhost:8080/actuator/health | jq
curl -s localhost:8080/v3/api-docs | jq '.paths | keys'

check.expect: Your two account paths are listed.

tasks.do: Log as JSON with a request id on every line
tasks.why: From step 04 there are two services. Following one user request through two log files is impossible unless every line carries the same id.
tasks.how: Boot 3.4+ ships a structured logging format, so no Logback XML is needed for the JSON part. The filter puts a request id into the MDC — a per-thread map that the logging framework copies onto every line — and returns it in a response header so you can search for it later. Step 14 replaces this id with a real trace id from OpenTelemetry; the shape stays the same.

blocks.label: application.yml — add the block
blocks.body:
logging:
  structured:
    format:
      console: ecs        # ecs | logstash | gelf
  level:
    io.ledgerflow: DEBUG

blocks.label: adapter/in/web/RequestIdFilter.java

check.expect: A request id in the response header, and the same id on the app's log lines for that request.

proof.expect: problem+json for the bad id, and all three test layers green.
proof.note: This service is now finished. You could ship it. Everything from here on is about what happens when there is more than one of them.

doneWhen: Three test layers are green, health and OpenAPI are served, errors come back as problem+json, and every log line carries a request id.

lessons.title: Services tool window
lessons.teach: Services shows your Docker containers and running Spring Boot apps in one tree — start, stop, and read logs there rather than juggling terminal tabs.
lessons.fallbackTip: docker compose ps / docker compose logs -f

lessons.title: HTTP client scratch
lessons.teach: Make a .http file and put your curl calls in it. They become runnable, version-controlled requests with environment variables for ports.
lessons.fallbackTip: Ultimate only. Community: keep using curl.
